**US stocks in play — 2026-10-28 (late-session intraday)**

- **Run time:** 2026-10-28 15:51 ET (cron fire). Discovery ran 15:52–15:56 ET; **official closing prints captured 16:01–16:08 ET** (`marketStatus: After-Hours`, last trade timestamps 4:01–4:08 PM ET).
- Session state: **RTH close (regular trading completed)**.
- **Slot:** `intraday` — not the skill's 09:50 `open` slot nor a 12:30 `midday` slot.
- A late-session fire, so **midday-scale floors** were applied (session $ volume ≥ ~$2M, move ≥ ~3%) and the chat surfaces only the top of the book.
- **Sort:** Tier A → Soft-A → TECH_WATCH → B → C; within tier, **session USD $ volume descending**.
- **Data as-of / lag:** closing price + settled volume = **Yahoo chart API** (regular-session bar, no after-hours contamination) for the 62 names it was pulled for, cross-checked against **TradingView's** post-close scanner settle and **Nasdaq `/info`** (`secondaryData` = the 4:00 PM official close once `marketStatus` flips to After-Hours).
- Discovery layer = Yahoo's four predefined mover lists (628 unique) **plus** the TradingView per-country scanner (1,263 rows post-close, 4,537 names inside the filter).
- Catalysts = SEC EDGAR 8-K Atom feed + submissions API item codes, company IR releases, PR Newswire RSS, and independent press/wire reads. Net discovery lag ≈ 0 on the close.
- **Scope:** 1,603 raw discovery candidates → **507 passed the liquidity floors** → **446 fully priced with a settled close** → 17 Tier A, 6 Soft-A, 15 TECH_WATCH, 21 Tier B, 1 Tier C.
- Full ranked screen with tiers: `2026-10-28-candidates.csv` (446 rows).

- **Read this first:** this was a *hawkish hold* Fed day and the tape barely moved — but the **dispersion underneath was the widest in months**.
- The FOMC held at 3.75–4.00% on a **10–2 vote with two dissents in favour of a hike** (Cook and Hammack), upgraded the economy from "solid" to **"strong"**, and pushed a December hike to ~85–90% priced;
- the 10-year rose 5bp to 5.047% and the 30-year to 5.338%. Indexes closed green (S&P +0.28%, NDX +0.55%, VIX **-3.77%** to 16.86) and credit was flat (HYG 0.00%).
- Inside that calm, a **single AI-infrastructure trade** — Oracle's Investor Day (+10.6%) and Vertiv's Q3 beat (+16.6%) —
- plus an overnight **SK hynix profit shock** re-rated the entire memory and data-centre supply chain, while **every name outside that trade got sold** on its own disappointed print.
- The single most important caveat is in **Source health**:
- this sandbox has **no TradingView-advanced or Yahoo Finance MCPs registered**, and the Nasdaq **halt feed was unreachable**, so LULD/limit status could not be confirmed for any name.

- **The macro driver of the day.** The FOMC left the target range at **3.75–4.00%** (as expected, ~90% priced), but the vote was **10–2 with Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissenting in favour of a 25bp hike**, and the statement upgraded activity from "solid" to **"strong"** while repeating that inflation "remains elevated." That combination is the market's worst kind:
- no decision to trade, but a clearly higher path. December is now treated as a foregone conclusion (~85–90% on FedWatch) after the September 25bp hike.
- The starting point was hot September CPI (**3.7% y/y, up from 3.4%; core 2.6% y/y; +0.6% m/m headline**) and September PPI at **6.3% y/y**, the steepest in four years.
- Rates responded accordingly: 2-year +3.9bp to **4.776%**, 10-year +5bp to **5.047%**, 30-year +3.8bp to **5.338%**. WTI crude added $2.94 to **$102.82**; the dollar was flat near 102.

- **Why the indexes are green but the day feels violent.** The FOMC was the 2:00 PM catalyst and it landed into a tape that had already re-rated on two overnight prints.
- The constructive side was entirely *AI infrastructure and memory*:
- SK hynix's sevenfold profit surge gave the semiconductor complex its catalyst, and Oracle's Investor Day did the same for data-centre power and cooling.
- The Fed then lifted the discount rate but could not dent the AI capex narrative. Everything else — software, homebuilders, logistics, consumer-discretionary restaurants, solar — sold its own news.
- **That is the whole day:** one trade up, the rest of the market down on idiosyncratic disappointment, with volatility *falling* because the vol market was trading the Fed, not the equity dispersion.

- **What Tier A actually says.** Seventeen names, and the pattern is unusually clean: **every one of them carries a same-session, filing-grade catalyst** —
- 2.02 earnings items, an Investor Day, a Phase 3 readout, or an M&A/strategic disclosure.
- Nine are earnings prints (VRT, FLEX, ICLR, EAT, LII, ENPH, STLA, CHRW, WING) and the rest are strategic (ORCL, AXGN, GMAB, CSGP) or a foreign issuer's record quarter (SKHY).
- Two observations matter more than the percentages:

- **Direction and quality are independent here.** The five biggest moves in the table are split between beats (VRT +16.6% , ICLR +17.0% , GMAB +28.3% ,
- AXGN +31.5%) and *misses that were still beaten on the headline* but sold on the guide (FFIV -20.4% , LPLA -15.2% , CHRW -11.1% , CSGP -14.0%).
- FFIV beat on revenue **and** EPS and still lost a fifth of its value, because the FY27 growth rate fell from 11% to 8–9% and the margin guide went the wrong way.
- Same with CHRW (+29.5% revenue) and CSGP (record EBITDA). **On a hawkish-hold Fed day with a 5% 10-year, the market paid only for the *forward* number.**
- **Close location is the tiebreaker inside each tier.** VRT closed 0.9% off its high and ICLR closed *on* its high;
- FFIV closed 1.0% off its low, LPLA closed on its low, and BSX closed 6.8% above its intraday low after touching -12%.
- The three names that faded from the high (ORCL -2.8% off its high, VRT -0.9% ,
- FLEX -0.7%) all gave back some of the move in the final hour on a hawkish-Fed tape.

- **Two names carry the highest information-per-dollar in the table and both deserve a position-size caveat.** **GMAB** is a +28.3% move on a single topline dataset that is genuinely good (HR 0.50, p<0.0001, both primary endpoints met) but comes with no RVol baseline on a newly-IPO'd ADR, a competitor's equity marked down the same minute, and full data still to come at a medical meeting —
- the JPM peak-sales estimate of $5B is an analyst's, not the company's.
- **AXGN** is +31.5% on a genuine beat-and-raise, but it also carries the dilution from a $225M offering priced at $42.50 to fund a $200M acquisition, and the stock is now a second-day re-rating off a ~16% one-month drawdown.
- Neither is a fault line; both are positions whose size should reflect *how much of the thesis is still unread*.

**Tier C — deal-risk / arbitrage, explicitly not momentum (1)**

- **Ticker**: WEN · **% chg**: +15.15% · **Last**: $7.07 · **$ vol**: $0.24B (+2 more column(s) in the artifact table)

- **Why this is quarantined.** The skill's buyout rule is explicit, and it applies cleanly here: a name trading near stated cash terms is **sideways arbitrage, not a chase**.
- WEN at 5.81× RVol and +15.2% looks like a momentum breakout on a screen. It is actually a **closed-ish spread** —
- and a *wide* one for a deal of this size, which is the tell that the market does not think $7.35 is a floor.
- Pre-bid market value was ~$1.17B; some retail holders are publicly arguing the bid undervalues the company and that the board should push for more.
- Until the board responds, this is a spread to monitor, not a position to size.

**Method & caveats**

- **Universe:** NYSE/NASDAQ/AMEX common stock plus major ETFs. Excluded: warrants, rights, units, preferreds, blank-check SPACs, and single-stock/leveraged ETFs.
- The blanket screens rejected 74 preferreds, 30 blank-check SPACs, 14 warrant/unit tickers, 11 sub-$1 names, 6 sub-$50M microcaps, 214 names below the $2M turnover floor and 289 names with a move under 3%.
- **Discovery coverage is two independent lists, not one.** Yahoo's four predefined mover lists returned **628 unique names** (day_gainers 178, day_losers 153, most_actives 273, small_cap_gainers 110) and the TradingView per-country scanner returned **1,263 rows across four sorts** inside a market-cap ≥$50M and price ≥$1 filter, out of 4,537 qualifying names.
- Merging both is what caught SKHY and GMAB — two of the day's largest moves — which a single curated list would likely have missed.
- The residual gap: a ≥5% mover that *both* lists omitted for any window could have been missed, and the 446-name priced set is a floor, not a census.
- **Liquidity floors applied (midday-scale, to a near-close print):** price ≥ $1; market cap ≥ $50M; session $ volume ≥ ~$2M; move ≥ ~3%.
- 1,603 raw candidates → 507 passed → 446 priced with a settled close.
- **RVol** = session volume ÷ 10-session average volume (TradingView `relative_volume_10d_calc` / `average_volume_10d_calc`).
- **Known denominator bias:** TradingView's 10-day average volume measures **6–16% tighter than Yahoo's trailing-10-session average** (measured across 12 symbols on 2026-10-28, median ~0.90×), so TV-based RVol is **overstated by roughly that margin** versus a Yahoo denominator.
- It is stated as the direction of the bias because it could flip a bucket.
- **SKHY and GMAB have no RVol baseline** (no TradingView average-volume history for either), and both are placed in Tier A under the pipeline rule that a missing RVol is not a disqualifier —
- but read them as unquantified, not as quiet.
- **Price-source discipline.** Three sources were compared for the closing print and they do not agree perfectly: **Yahoo chart API** (regular-session bar), **TradingView's** post-close scanner settle, and **Nasdaq `/info`**.
- Nine names diverged by more than 1.2% on price or 1.0pp on percentage change between sources, and **Nasdaq was the one that failed** —
- its `primaryData` switches to the *after-hours* print within seconds of the close, so a naive fetch after 16:00 returns the AH price with an AH percentage while the field still says "Open".
- The fix was to read `secondaryData` once `marketStatus` flips to `After-Hours`, and to treat **Yahoo's regular-session bar as authoritative** with TradingView as the cross-check.
- All quoted closes and percentage changes in this digest are the **official regular-session settle**; after-hours prints are excluded by construction. Settlement lag: closing prints captured 16:01–16:08 ET.
- **Session $ volume** = official close × settled full-day share volume.
- The first pass used a pre-close (15:52 ET) volume snapshot, which understated the heaviest names by up to ~30% (MU, for example) and would have mis-ranked the top of the book;
- the column above uses settled volume throughout, with the source recorded per row in the CSV.
- **Tier rules applied.** Tier A = floors + material same-session catalyst (direction-agnostic — a beat-and-raise that sold, like FFIV, qualifies, and so does a miss that was bought, like STLA).
- Soft-A = high-material same-session catalyst with *known-soft or missing* RVol. TECH_WATCH = floors + soft-trigger move + real turnover, no same-session catalyst, RVol ~0.5–2.0×.
- Tier B = floors + move, weak or no catalyst. Tier C = deal-risk/arb only. RVol was deliberately **not** a hard gate at any point, per the US-slot rule.
- **Buyout rule enforced:** WEN was kept out of the momentum tiers despite 5.81× RVol and a +15.2% move, because the stock closed *below* the stated $7.35 cash terms.
- **Unverified items are labelled, not smoothed over.** EVR's beat and consensus come from a single earnings-calendar source; ODFL's, LCII's and APH's headline figures were not verified against filings;
- WING's +12.2% move has no located analyst explanation; LOGI, SLS, VSAT and AXTI have no verified same-session catalyst;
- the big-tech Q3 prints (META, GOOGL, MSFT) were not verified in this run;
- and ORCL's non-Investor-Day figures come from the Oct 27 digest's reported Q1 FY27 print, not from today's release.
- **Pre-market annex:** not produced — a 15:51 ET fire makes pre-market gap data stale, and the same reasoning applies to a 16:00 ET close.
- **MCP availability:** `tool_search` returns **zero** registered `mcp__tradingview_advanced__*` or `mcp__yahoo_finance__*` tools in this sandbox.
- The skill's TradingView budget (≤12–15 MCP calls/slot) was therefore not applicable and no screener/news MCP corroboration was possible.
- The **MCP-over-HTTP bridge was used successfully** for the session's SPY context (StockTwits daily bars, 23 sessions) and served as an independent check that the tape was live.
- Every catalyst in this digest is filing-grade (EDGAR 8-K item codes), company-IR-grade (issuer press releases), or wire-grade (Reuters, CNBC, Barron's, Bloomberg, WSJ, AFP, PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire, Business Wire).
- **FYI on a data trap that was avoided:** several widely-circulated "top movers" pages dated Oct 28 were found to be **recycling the Oct 27 move** —
- "CBRS +10.10% on Oracle offering Cerebras inference" and "XYL -14.21% on a Q3 miss" are both Oct 27 events.
- On Oct 28 CBRS closed **-5.66%** (a give-back) and XYL closed **-4.98%** (a second-day drift). Every catalyst in this digest was re-dated to its actual session before publication.
